[1/4] Two doc/registry contradictions found; plan the coherent fix

impact_assessment.why: knowledge/state_machines.md and scripts/state_machines.py disagree on two machines. The doc's Proof verdict row claims unproven/holds/refused, none of which appear in proof_gate.py (the CLI contract is 0 proof holds / 1 proof failed / 2 setup); the registry machine actually named proof-verdict carries the shared-outcome vocabulary instead. The doc's Receipt/corpus row says not-persisted while the registry and code say absent.
impact_assessment.benefits: One name maps to one vocabulary, so an agent that reads the doc and then queries --machine gets the same states; the inventory stops asserting two different things about the same concept.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: scripts/state_machines.py machine names and states, the --machine CLI; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: state_machines.py, knowledge/state_machines.md, tests/test_kit.py, an ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: verify every rename/add against the code that produces the vocabulary; keep a compatibility note in the ADR; pin with tests that read the doc and the module; run both tiers and the full gate set

[1/4] Verify every registry gap claim; two are stale

impact_assessment.why: Each machine records a known gap, and readers treat those as live defects. Two are now false: reforge-run says completed->stopped is refused with no clear status output, but it emits a full Why/Fix triad (measured), and dossier-catalogue says two paths both return False when sync_published returns dicts with distinct skipped reasons. A stale gap sends a developer to fix a defect that no longer exists.
impact_assessment.benefits: The gap field becomes trustworthy, so the next reader spends time on the real defects and the registry stops misreporting the code.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: scripts/state_machines.py gap strings and the doc's Enforcement/gap column; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: state_machines.py, knowledge/state_machines.md, tests, an ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: measure each gap against the code before editing; keep the live half of a partly-stale gap; pin the corrected claims with tests that read the modules

[1/2] Pin the untested review-lease ledger

impact_assessment.why: The idea-repo-review gap states the whole lease ledger has no tests; a grep confirmed zero references to release_expired, stale_reviews, reserved_ids, validate_reviews or _lease_expired in either tier. The lease decides which idea numbers parallel dossier sessions may claim, so an untested bug corrupts a shared register.
impact_assessment.benefits: Reservation, expiry, abandonment, idempotent release and forced takeover become pinned, so a later change cannot silently corrupt the register.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, tests only; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: tests/test_kit.py, the registry gap text, an ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: write each pin from the implementation, correct any assumption the first run contradicts, keep the gap text to what remains true, and run both tiers plus every gate

[1/3] Make --audit create no directory when the ledger is absent

impact_assessment.why: run_disruption_audit calls get_ledger_path solely to compute a path when no ledger exists, and that helper unconditionally mkdirs the memory directory. Measured with --workspace on an empty dir: the audit creates .agents (empty). A read-only audit that writes a directory is an AX and DX defect: a probe, a health check or an agent's first look mutates the workspace it was asked to inspect.
impact_assessment.benefits: An absent ledger no longer causes a write, so any caller can probe a workspace without changing it; the quarantine-on-corrupt behaviour stays, because that is lossless recovery of damaged data.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: run_disruption_audit return values and the --audit CLI; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: disruption_recovery.py, tests, an ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: compute the path without the mkdir side effect instead of changing get_ledger_path itself, which write paths rely on; pin both the absent-ledger and corrupt-ledger cases; run both tiers and every gate
